cues.text: To coincide with the 1964 Tokyo Olympics,
cues.en: To coincide with the 1964 Tokyo Olympics,
cues.zh: 為配合 1964 年東京奧運會，

cues.text: Japan launched the world’s first high-speed train, the Shinkansen.
cues.en: Japan launched the world’s first high-speed train, the Shinkansen.

cues.text: Capable of running at 210 kph,
cues.en: Capable of running at 210 kph,
cues.zh: 行進時速能達到兩百一十公里，

cues.text: this groundbreaking bullet train inspired countries around the world
cues.en: this groundbreaking bullet train inspired countries around the world
cues.zh: 這種開創性的子彈列車 鼓舞了世界各國

cues.text: to invest in high-speed rail.
cues.en: to invest in high-speed rail.

cues.text: Today, these trains regularly travel at over 300 kph,
cues.en: Today, these trains regularly travel at over 300 kph,
cues.zh: 現今，這類高速鐵路列車的時速 通常都超過三百公里，

cues.text: on par with the takeoff speed of a commercial airplane.
cues.en: on par with the takeoff speed of a commercial airplane.
cues.zh: 和民航客機的起飛速度不相上下。

cues.en: But could these trains go even faster,

cues.text: whisking passengers to their destinations quicker than the smoothest flight?
cues.en: whisking passengers to their destinations quicker than the smoothest flight?
cues.zh: 讓乘客比搭乘最順暢的航班 還快抵達目的地？

cues.en: To answer this, it helps to understand
cues.zh: 要回答這個問題，最好先了解

cues.text: how these trains reach their already impressive speeds.
cues.en: how these trains reach their already impressive speeds.
cues.zh: 這些列車是如何達到如此驚人的速度。

cues.text: There are three main factors that separate bullet trains
cues.en: There are three main factors that separate bullet trains
cues.zh: 子彈列車與傳統低速列車的 差別在於三個因素：

cues.text: from traditional, low-speed trains:
cues.en: from traditional, low-speed trains:
cues.zh: 引擎、空氣動力學，和基礎設施。

cues.text: engines, aerodynamics, and infrastructure.
cues.en: engines, aerodynamics, and infrastructure.
cues.zh: 引擎、空氣動力學，和基礎設施。

cues.text: Most traditional trains are powered by combustion engines,
cues.en: Most traditional trains are powered by combustion engines,
cues.zh: 大多數傳統列車的動力 都來自燃燒引擎，

cues.text: which combust fuel— typically diesel— to turn an electric generator.
cues.en: which combust fuel— typically diesel— to turn an electric generator.
cues.zh: 這類引擎靠燃燒燃料——通常是柴油——

cues.text: This electricity is then used to power motors that turn the train’s wheels.
cues.en: This electricity is then used to power motors that turn the train’s wheels.
cues.zh: 產生的電力則用來驅動馬達， 讓火車的車輪轉動起來。

cues.text: High-speed trains, on the other hand,
cues.en: High-speed trains, on the other hand,
cues.zh: 另一方面，高速列車

cues.text: use electric engines to power their motors.
cues.en: use electric engines to power their motors.
cues.zh: 使用電動引擎來驅動馬達。

cues.text: This process is more energy efficient than combustion
cues.en: This process is more energy efficient than combustion
cues.zh: 比起燃燒燃料，這種流程更節能，

cues.text: and allows train operators to reach top speeds more quickly.
cues.en: and allows train operators to reach top speeds more quickly.
cues.zh: 且列車駕駛員能更快達到最高速度。

cues.text: Next up is aerodynamics.
cues.en: Next up is aerodynamics.
cues.zh: 下一個因素是空氣動力學。

cues.text: While low- and high-speed trains use the same steel wheels
cues.en: While low- and high-speed trains use the same steel wheels
cues.zh: 低速列車和高速列車 都使用相同的鋼輪，

cues.text: to minimize friction with the track,
cues.en: to minimize friction with the track,
cues.zh: 把輪子和軌道的摩擦減到最小，

cues.text: bullet trains are also designed with aerodynamic bodies
cues.en: bullet trains are also designed with aerodynamic bodies
cues.zh: 但子彈列車的車體設計 還運用了空氣動力學，

cues.text: that slice through air with minimal resistance.
cues.en: that slice through air with minimal resistance.
cues.zh: 車體能切開空氣， 讓空氣阻力減到最小。

cues.text: Engineers could use these slicker designs on traditional train cars.
cues.en: Engineers could use these slicker designs on traditional train cars.
cues.zh: 工程師可以把這類流線的設計 放在傳統列車車廂上。

cues.text: But while upgrading to electric engines
cues.en: But while upgrading to electric engines
cues.zh: 雖然升級成電力引擎

cues.text: would make low-speed trains more efficient,
cues.en: would make low-speed trains more efficient,
cues.zh: 確實能提升低速列車的效能，

cues.text: they wouldn't get much benefit from these aerodynamic designs
cues.en: they wouldn't get much benefit from these aerodynamic designs
cues.zh: 但空氣動力學的設計 卻對它們幫助不大，

cues.text: because of the third factor: infrastructure.
cues.en: because of the third factor: infrastructure.
cues.zh: 原因就是第三個因素：基礎設施。

cues.text: Traditional train tracks were built to meet people where they lived,
cues.en: Traditional train tracks were built to meet people where they lived,
cues.zh: 傳統鐵路軌道的建置， 主要考量人們居住的地點，

cues.text: ensuring stations were accessible to any potential passengers.
cues.en: ensuring stations were accessible to any potential passengers.
cues.zh: 讓可能需要搭乘的乘客方便到達車站。

cues.text: But to prevent derailments in these highly populated areas,
cues.en: But to prevent derailments in these highly populated areas,
cues.zh: 但為了防止列車 在人口稠密的地區脫軌，

cues.text: trains need to frequently decelerate to safely hit turns and cross roads.
cues.en: trains need to frequently decelerate to safely hit turns and cross roads.
cues.zh: 在轉彎和經過路口時， 為了安全，列車經常需要減速。

cues.text: High-speed rails, on the other hand, were built to prioritize speed.
cues.en: High-speed rails, on the other hand, were built to prioritize speed.
cues.zh: 相較之下，高速列車軌道的建置 把速度列為優先考量。

cues.text: They run on long, straight lines that avoid road crossings,
cues.en: They run on long, straight lines that avoid road crossings,
cues.zh: 路線通常又長又直， 且會避免與道路交會，

cues.text: sharp curves, and high traffic areas.
cues.en: sharp curves, and high traffic areas.
cues.zh: 盡量不使用彎道， 不經過交通繁忙的地區。

cues.text: These three differences allow high-speed trains
cues.en: These three differences allow high-speed trains
cues.zh: 這三項差異讓高速列車

cues.text: to reach top speeds over double their traditional counterparts.
cues.en: to reach top speeds over double their traditional counterparts.
cues.zh: 速度能飆到傳統列車的兩倍以上。

cues.text: And since their infrastructure allows them to travel longer distances between stops,
cues.en: And since their infrastructure allows them to travel longer distances between stops,
cues.zh: 由於高速列車的基礎設施 讓站與站間的距離可以更長，

cues.text: they spend more time cruising near top speed,
cues.en: they spend more time cruising near top speed,
cues.zh: 列車用接近最高速 行駛的時間也比較長，

cues.text: often traveling up to three times the average speed of traditional trains.
cues.en: often traveling up to three times the average speed of traditional trains.
cues.zh: 行駛速度高達傳統列車 平均速度的三倍。

cues.text: But new technology is emerging to make even faster trains.
cues.en: But new technology is emerging to make even faster trains.
cues.zh: 但，更多新技術不斷出現， 讓列車的速度還能更快。

cues.text: To eliminate friction between rails and wheels,
cues.en: To eliminate friction between rails and wheels,
cues.zh: 為了消除軌道和輪子之間的摩擦，

cues.text: engineers have developed new magnetic levitation, or maglev, trains.
cues.en: engineers have developed new magnetic levitation, or maglev, trains.
cues.zh: 工程師已經開發出了 新型磁懸浮列車或磁浮列車。

cues.text: There are two major approaches here.
cues.en: There are two major approaches here.
cues.zh: 用到的方法主要有兩種。

cues.text: In electromagnetic suspension,
cues.en: In electromagnetic suspension,
cues.zh: 在電磁懸浮系統中，

cues.text: magnetized arms wrap under the track and pull the train up.
cues.en: magnetized arms wrap under the track and pull the train up.
cues.zh: 軌道下方環繞著磁化的支臂， 能將列車向上拉起。

cues.text: Meanwhile, in electrodynamic suspension,
cues.en: Meanwhile, in electrodynamic suspension,
cues.zh: 而在電動力懸浮系統中，

cues.text: coils embedded in the track create a pattern of alternating magnetic fields
cues.en: coils embedded in the track create a pattern of alternating magnetic fields
cues.zh: 內建在軌道中的線圈， 會產生交替變化的磁場，

cues.text: that interact with magnets on the train
cues.en: that interact with magnets on the train
cues.zh: 和列車上的磁場產生互動作用，

cues.text: to float the vehicle a few centimeters in the air.
cues.en: to float the vehicle a few centimeters in the air.
cues.zh: 讓列車能浮在空中，離地幾公分。

cues.text: To change speed,
cues.en: To change speed,
cues.zh: 要改變列車速度時，

cues.text: train operators alternate the direction of the trains’ magnetic field,
cues.en: train operators alternate the direction of the trains’ magnetic field,
cues.zh: 列車操作員會轉換列車的磁場方向，

cues.text: attracting the front of the train to the next coil to speed up
cues.en: attracting the front of the train to the next coil to speed up
cues.zh: 利用磁力將列車前端 拉向下一個線圈，

cues.text: or reversing the field’s phase to brake.
cues.en: or reversing the field’s phase to brake.
cues.zh: 反轉磁場的相位則可以煞車。

cues.text: Given enough runway,
cues.en: Given enough runway,
cues.zh: 若有足夠的加速距離，

cues.text: these trains can reach speeds from 430
cues.en: these trains can reach speeds from 430
cues.zh: 磁浮列車的時速 可高達四百三十公里，

cues.text: to a theoretical 600 kph,

cues.zh: 理論上甚至能衝到六百公里。

cues.text: allowing them to make the over 4,400 kilometer trip
cues.en: allowing them to make the over 4,400 kilometer trip
cues.zh: 因此，若行駛超過 四千四百公里的距離，

cues.text: from New York City to Los Angeles in as little as seven hours.
cues.en: from New York City to Los Angeles in as little as seven hours.
cues.zh: 從紐約市一路行駛到洛杉磯， 也僅需要七小時。

cues.en: So why haven’t we built maglev trains, or even high-speed trains, everywhere?
cues.zh: 那為什麼我們不到處建置 磁浮列車或甚至更高速的列車？

cues.en: most of which is needed to overcome air resistance.

cues.zh: 事實上，在時速三百公里的情況下，

cues.en: and several projects currently in development
